- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% to prevent overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent low trend.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model often fails to catch the momentum; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment shift by 2–5%.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates volatility; cap forecast range within ±10% of 14-day moving average to avoid extreme outliers.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment polarity shift.
